Looking into that. So far so good, no major issues!" 5GB DAG estimated for August 19, which will make a lot of ASICS obsolete and will affect TTD if it’s set before this date While I'm glad the Sepolia issues weren't technical but rather "social" it does concern me that roughly 1/4th of the validators couldn't apply a rather simple update to the final TTD and/or clients. The whole point of making Sepolia permissioned was that the validator set would all be vested in keeping the network running but that doesn't really seem to be the case. Yeah agree, we will look into how we can make it even easier, clearer how to set up nodes and how to run validators Best case would probably be a release with the correct TTD preconfigured If entities running permissioned validator set missed the memo, I would imagine it would be worse for normal users I think a list of common pitfalls and what to look for in the logs to know things are configured correctly would go a long way to reduce these issues. which we will be doing for mainnet and goerli. we just had to do the ttd override stuff due to pow testnets having low hashrates. 💯 For mainnet, given the upperlimit on possible increases to hashrate and the likelyhood of a decent hashrate dropoff, we should pick a TTD on the smaller side. IMHO, a potentially shorter than desirable upgrade window with only a single simple client upgrade is much more desirable than having to do a TTD override or multiple client releases with different TTDs. I think mainnet will be way different. When there is real money at stake everyone cares about their validators. Another approach -- optimize choice of TTD/timing of TTD announcement with an optimization-view of that having a higher cost than has been effectively assumed so far, i.e. try as much as feasible to set a TTD that one can stick with, the first time. Sure, it was difficult with these testnets with so little hashrate people could come in with 10x or 30x the hashrate individually, but on mainnet (and to a lesser extent goerli) it should be possible to arrange a TTD robust to this. Yeah, that's much more realistic on mainnet. One risk with this is the hashrate drops and a TTD we expect to hit in, say, 3 weeks, ends up being hit in 4-5 because the difficulty has gone down. Is a drop in hashrate to be expected or are miners planning on mining until last PoW block? Too early to say <@453080919255941139>! The first post-merge epoch finalized with a consistent participation rate compared to pre-merge, which is a great sign! But the second epoch post-merge has a lower participation rate, and devs are looking into why that is. Could be because of something as silly as the monitoring systems having a problem, or something more nefarious, too early to tell. 

You can follow via this URL: https://sepolia.beaconcha.in/charts/slotviz and here: https://sepolia.beaconcha.in/epochs

First post-merge epoch was 3600, you can see it finalized with 94.52% participation, compared to 94.57% pre-merge (epoch 3599). As per Danny Ryan, consistency is key here, so that's promising! But second epoch (3601) participation dropped to  68.48%. That's still enough for the chain to finalize (need to be more than 66%), so that's good, but obviously that number should be higher! Will wait for more info from devs!
